hints: Notice the key condition, ethanolic sodium hydroxide favours elimination to form C=C double bonds, not substitution by OH.
Start from $\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ and remove one $\text{HBr}$ from each C-Br end to form the first alkene, then repeat it.
With excess reagent both bromine atoms are lost as $\text{HBr}$, leaving a $\text{C}_4$ chain with two double bonds, so work out $M_r$ for $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reagent type**

Ethanolic NaOH causes dehydrohalogenation (elimination of HBr). Aqueous NaOH would cause substitution to an alcohol, but that is not used here.

Rule:
$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{OH}^- \text{(ethanolic)} \rightarrow \text{R-CH=CH}_2 + \text{Br}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Apply double elimination**

1,4-dibromobutane has two C-Br groups: $\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. With excess reagent, both undergo elimination.

$$\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{=CH-CH=CH}_2 + 2\text{HBr}$$
The major organic product is buta-1,3-diene.

**Calculate the relative formula mass**

Buta-1,3-diene is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$.

$$M_r = (4 \times 12.0) + (6 \times 1.0) = 48 + 6 = 54$$

options.A: Correct. Double dehydrobromination gives buta-1,3-diene, $\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-CH=CH}_2$. Its formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$ so $M_r = 54$.
options.B: Incorrect. 56 is $M_r$ of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$ such as butene or cyclobutane, with only one C=C bond. This comes from stopping after only one elimination, but excess reagent removes both HBr molecules to give two double bonds.
options.C: Incorrect. 74 is $M_r$ of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ such as butanol. This is the trap of confusing ethanolic NaOH (elimination) with aqueous NaOH (substitution to alcohol).
options.D: Incorrect. 90 is $M_r$ of butane-1,4-diol, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$). That would be the product of substitution with aqueous NaOH, not elimination with ethanolic NaOH.
